chapterName: Late Republic: Caesar's Civil War and the Ides of March (49-44 BCE)

questions.question: Why did Brutus refuse to have Mark Antony killed along with Caesar?
options: Antony had secretly joined the plot
He feared Antony's legions in Gaul
Antony was away fighting the Parthians
Antony was his brother-in-law
Killing only Caesar looked like removing a tyrant
questions.explanation: Brutus argued that killing only Caesar would look like removing a tyrant rather than a purge. Antony later brokered the compromise after the murder.
questions.sourceQuote: Brutus refused, arguing that killing only Caesar would look like removing a tyrant rather than a purge.

questions.question: According to an anecdote, how did Caesar handle tripping as he landed in Africa?
options: He sacrificed a bull to cancel the omen
He sailed back and landed further along
He ordered his officers to keep it secret
He seized sand, claiming to have hold of Africa
He postponed the invasion for three days
questions.explanation: Caesar laughed off the bad omen by grabbing sand and crying, "I have hold of you, Africa!"
questions.sourceQuote: According to an anecdote, Caesar tripped on landing and laughed off the bad omen by grabbing sand and crying, "I have hold of you, Africa!"

questions.question: What was Caesar presented with when he reached Alexandria after Pompey's death? (select all that apply)
options: Pompey's last letter
Pompey's sword
Pompey's head
Pompey's signet ring
Pompey's war chest
questions.explanation: Caesar was given Pompey's head and signet ring. He wept at the ring and recoiled from the head, though historians debate whether his grief was genuine.
questions.sourceQuote: Julius Caesar reached Alexandria, Egypt's capital, three days later and was presented with Pompey's head and signet ring.

questions.question: Why did the plotters choose a Senate meeting for the assassination?
options: Caesar's friends could not protect him there
The tribunes had promised to help
The meeting would be held at night
Mark Antony was certain to be absent
It was held in a temple of Jupiter
questions.explanation: At a Senate meeting Caesar's friends could not protect him. The Ides of March meeting was the last before he left to fight the Parthians.
questions.sourceQuote: They chose a Senate meeting, where Caesar's friends could not protect him.

questions.question: Why did senators take offence when a delegation brought Caesar new honours?
options: He refused the honours outright
He demanded a royal diadem instead
He had the delegation arrested
He stayed seated when etiquette demanded he stand
He kept them waiting outside for hours
questions.explanation: Caesar stayed seated and joked that his honours should be cut back. It looked as if he no longer cared about the Senate.
questions.sourceQuote: Etiquette demanded he stand; he stayed seated and joked that his honours should be cut back.

questions.question: After the garrison at Corfinium surrendered, what did Caesar do?
options: Let his legions plunder the town freely
Freed the senators and returned soldiers' pay
Sold the garrison soldiers into slavery
Sent the prisoners east in chains
Executed the senators among the garrison
questions.explanation: Caesar freed some fifty senators and noblemen and even returned the soldiers' pay. This shrewd clemency kept Italy from turning on him.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar freed some fifty senators and noblemen and even returned the soldiers' pay.

questions.question: What did Caesar do that angered ordinary Romans after some in a crowd hailed him as king?
options: Had the arresting tribunes stripped of office
Accepted the title of rex
Banned public gatherings in the Forum
Had the shouting man executed
Raised taxes on the city's poor
questions.explanation: The tribunes arrested the first man to shout "king", and Caesar responded by removing them from office, which angered ordinary Romans.
questions.sourceQuote: When the tribunes arrested the first man to shout, Caesar had them stripped of office, angering ordinary Romans.

questions.question: What did Caesar want to secure before giving up his army?
options: A second term as consul
Command of a war against Parthia
Pompey's exile from Rome
A triumph for his Gallic wars
Control of the state treasury
questions.explanation: Caesar wanted a second consulship before disarming, while Pompey and the hardliners demanded he disarm first.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar wanted a second term as consul, Rome's highest office, before giving up his army.

questions.question: What did Caesar say he was defending by going to war?
options: Pompey's safety in Rome
Rome's grain supply
The Senate's emergency authority
His personal honour, or dignitas
The rights of Rome's Gallic allies
questions.explanation: Caesar framed the war as a defence of his dignitas. Pride on both sides seems to have tipped Rome into war.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar said he was defending his personal honour (*dignitas*).

questions.question: Where did the Second Triumvirate defeat Brutus in 42 BC?
options: Actium
Dyrrachium
Philippi
Munda
Pharsalus
questions.explanation: The triumvirs beat Brutus at Philippi in northern Greece. They also declared Caesar a god and revived murderous purges.
questions.sourceQuote: They declared Caesar a god, revived murderous purges of their enemies, and defeated Brutus at Philippi, in northern Greece, in 42 BC.
